note: Append-only. Each entry carries the hash of the one before it. The log proves nothing about events before entry 1.

anchor.how_to_check: Fetch /repos/arcifact/arcifact-site/events, find the PushEvent whose payload.head is the commit that introduced the head you care about, and read its created_at. GitHub sets that when it accepts the push. Then fetch commitments.json at that exact commit and confirm its signed head matches. verify_report.py --online does all of this and fails if any part does not bind.
anchor.why_not_git_dates: A commit's author and committer dates are set by whoever makes the commit and evidence nothing about publication. An earlier version of this file recommended reading them. That was wrong; do not use them.
limits: GitHub exposes repository events for up to 30 days and at most 300 events, so this is a time-limited independent check rather than a durable one
it evidences when the push was received, not who authored the commit: these commits are unsigned
every timestamp inside this file is issuer-stated. Only the push event is third party

a durable anchor would be a signed commit carrying GitHub's persistent verified_at. That is not in place: the credential in use cannot register a signing key, and commits made through the API were tested and come back unsigned
checking it needs network access, so offline verification reports the public chronology as not checked rather than as passed

entries.claim: The expression evaluator that decides fail-open predicates. Committed separately because a change here changes what the analyser can conclude.

entries.subject: arcifact-report/1 envelope schema
entries.claim: The record format every instrument emits. Committed so a future record cannot claim conformance to a schema that was quietly altered.

entries.subject: Gate finding bar, from this date
entries.claim: A Gate finding is only reported as a proven gap when: the gate is an enforced required check resolved from a supplied required-check list; the uncovered job is not in needs, not reachable to the gate, and has no inspected dependent; the job is not marked continue-on-error; and the finding reproduces in both exact and closure modes. Anything else is reported as advisory, unresolved, or not analysed.

entries.subject: Gate cli.py
entries.claim: Analyser bytes in force from this entry. Supersedes entry 6. Adds inert gates, tolerant comparisons, status-function misuse, gates inspecting nothing, fail-fast compounds, orphan contexts, matrix naming and unread subgraphs.

entries.subject: Gate counterexample.py
entries.claim: Counterexample synthesiser. Constructs a concrete world in which the uncovered job fails and the gate is green, then evaluates the gate's own condition under it and emits nothing if the gate would go red.

entries.subject: Gate sensitivity.py
entries.claim: Sensitivity prober. Injects known faults into a workflow and checks each is reported, with negative controls that must produce no false gap.

entries.subject: Gate repo.py
entries.claim: Repository-level closure. Expands local reusable workflows, finds callee jobs that cannot fail their caller, and resolves required contexts across all workflows.

entries.claim: Engine bytes in force from this entry.

entries.subject: Gate gexpr.py
entries.claim: Engine bytes in force from this entry.

entries.subject: Counterexample bar, from this entry
entries.claim: A counterexample is emitted only when the gate's own condition, evaluated under the constructed world by the expression engine, leaves the gate green. If the gate would go red, or the condition cannot be modelled, nothing is emitted. Assumptions about other jobs' outputs are recorded in the counterexample itself.

entries.subject: Gate build manifest (all producing modules)
entries.claim: A single digest over the sha256 of every module that can produce a Gate record: cli.py, core.py, gexpr.py, counterexample.py, repo.py, sensitivity.py. Listing two files by hand let a record carry evidence from components it did not name. A record issued after this entry binds this manifest.
